summary: Barbra R. Clayton works in Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at McGill University (attested 2001) under doctoral supervisors Richard P. Hayes and Katherine K. Young, and also studied under G. Raj. She held a post at Mount Allison University (attested 2013).
Barend A. van Nooten is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Murray Barnson Emeneau. He held a post at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2007).

Barend Faddegon was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Amsterdam and Leiden University (PhD, until 1906) under C. C. Uhlenbeck, J. H. C. Kern, and J. S. Speyer. He served at Amsterdam (1908–1944) and Harvard (1926–1927).

Barend J. ter Haar is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed his PhD at Leiden University (until 1990) under Erik Zürcher and Susan Naquin. He held positions at KNAW, Heidelberg, Leiden (c. 2000–2013), and Hamburg (c. 2018).

Barend Jan Terwiel works in history, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Utrecht University and the Australian National University (PhD 1972). He held posts at the Royal Tropical Institute, ANU, Munich, Hamburg (1992–2007), and Leiden (1999–2004).

Barry Kerzin works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at UC Berkeley, USC (MD 1976), and under Geshe Namgyal Wangchen. He held posts at the University of Washington (1985–1989), Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (2006), and University of Hong Kong (2014–2022).

Barry Tse works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Federation University Australia, the University of Queensland, the University of Liverpool, and James Cook University Singapore (PhD 2021–2025). He held posts at James Cook University Singapore and the University of Newcastle.

Bart Dessein specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and philosophy. He studied Chinese at Liaoning University and earned his PhD at Ghent University (1990–1994) under Charles Willemen, where he was appointed Associate Professor in 1990.

Barthold Georg Niebuhr was a historian who studied at Kiel University (c. 1794–1796). He held academic chairs at the Humboldt University of Berlin (c. 1810–1816) and the University of Bonn (c. 1823–1831).
Basil Gould was a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics who studied at New College, University of Oxford (c. 1902–1906). He entered the Indian Civil Service in 1907.

Basil Lanneau Gildersleeve was a linguist who studied at Princeton, Bonn, and Göttingen (Dr. phil. 1853), learning under F. W. Ritschl and F. W. Schneidewin. He was professor of Greek at the University of Virginia (1856–1876) and Johns Hopkins University (1876–1915).

Batakrishna Ghosh was an Indologist and linguist who studied under doctoral supervisor Hanns Oertel (c. 1932–1935). He served as librarian at the Namgyal Institute of Tibetology and editor of the Bulletin of Tibetology.

Bazar Baradiin was a scholar of Buddhist, Tibetan, and Central Asian studies. Educated at Saint Petersburg State University, he taught there (1908–1917) and held leadership roles at the Buryat Scientific Center, Buryat State Pedagogical Institute, and the Institute of Oriental Studies.

Beata Grant is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from Stanford University and held academic positions at the University of California, Berkeley (c. 1987–1989) and Washington University in St. Louis (c. 1989).

Beatrice Erskine Lane worked in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Radcliffe College under William James, Josiah Royce, George Santayana, and George Herbert Palmer, then at Columbia University (MA). She held a professorship at Otani University from 1921.

Beatrix Pfleiderer worked in Indology and related fields. She studied at the University of Maryland and Heidelberg University, later holding posts at Maryland, Heidelberg, the University of Hamburg (1982), European University Viadrina, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Bedika Rai is a scholar in Buddhist studies. She served as an Assistant Professor at Salesian College (2010–2019) and at Kalipada Ghosh Tarai Mahavidyalaya (appointed 2019).

Bedřich Hrozný was a linguist and historian. He studied at the University of Vienna (PhD 1901) and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at the University of Vienna (from 1905) and Charles University (from 1919).
Bedřich Votýpka was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Charles University (1885–1892) under Josef Zubatý. He worked as a gymnasium professor at Gymnázium Benešov.

Beier Wang works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. Wang studied at the University of Toronto, the University of Hong Kong, and the University of Leipzig (PhD 2021), where Wang served as a Research Assistant from 2022 to 2025.
